what: Last harness fixes (atomic A1, CUT refused before logging, exit status, wraps, frozen sha checks), engineer report, workflow wf_71cd7408-a56

done.item: Fix 1 (vhi_guard.py): the A1 declaration check is now atomic
done.how: The path rule stays first: realpath(LOOK_DECLARED) must equal DECLARED_PATH, checked before anything is opened. Then declaration_check opens the file once with os.open(O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC). Links are followed, because a link to the protocol is allowed. _protocol_identity accepts the open file only if os.fstat(fd) has the st_dev and st_ino of os.stat(DECLARED_PATH) and of os.lstat(DECLARED_PATH). The protocol's own entry must be a regular file, and DECLARED_PATH must have no linked component. The text is read from that same descriptor. In resolve_cut (new resolve_cut_declared), an open file that is not the protocol is refused with the tag '(A1, atomic)' and closed without being read. look.plan now records the very declaration it judged (one read). open_run judges again just before the access line and stores it; it is written in the meta as declaration_check_at_open_run. resolve_cut keeps its old signature.
done.proof: lab/results/r2/validation_hi/proof_i_guard.json, rows 'A1 atomic (fix 1): ...' (11 rows, 0 failed). Every probe uses a stand-in text for the protocol: vhi_guard.DECLARED_PATH is pointed at it and restored in finally; the real protocol is never used. 3 controls: the stand-in by its path is accepted; a link to it with no race is accepted; a harness-output stand-in is refused by the path rule, and its own text passes the content rule. 4 deterministic races are now REFUSED. (1) The reviewer's race: a link that points to the stand-in when the path rule runs is re-pointed to a harness output right after it. A row shows the race happened, and that the old logic (re-open by name) would have accepted it. (2) The same race onto the real proofs.json with this spec's sha256; proofs.json alone passes the content rule. (3) The stand-in's own entry replaced by a link (caught by lstat). (4) A directory of its path replaced by a link (caught by the no-link check). End to end in a child process: row 'entry (child process ...): fix 1: LOOK_DECLARED = a link to the stand-in, re-pointed ... REFUSED (A1, atomic), nothing logged, no marker'. Also the plan_tests row 'fix 1: plan records the declaration it judged ...'.

done.item: Fix 2 (look.py plan, vhi_guard.look_cut_check): a look CUT other than the end of the look window is refused before anything is logged
done.how: plan() first calls G.look_cut_check(cut, spec). For 2022-01-01 < CUT <= 2026-01-01, the CUT must equal spec['windows']['look']['eval'][1], which is 2026-01-01. Any other CUT gets: 'CUT ... is refused for the look: a look runs only at the end of the spec's look window, CUT 2026-01-01 (...). Nothing was logged and no marker was written. Check --cut: the look's command uses --cut 2026-01-01.' A spec without a look window is refused for a look. This happens before the declared file is read and before open_run. A CUT after 2026-01-01 is still refused by resolve_cut (the holdout rule).
done.proof: proof_i_guard.json, child-process rows (vhi_run stubbed; the access log and look folder in the scratch folder; LOOK_DECLARED set in the child only, to the stand-in). 'fix 2: --cut 2024-01-01 with a valid declaration (the stand-in): REFUSED ...' and the same for --cut 2025-12-31: exit 1, 0 log lines, no marker, guard not installed, run_spec not reached. 'look.py --cut 2024-01-01 (the real spec) without LOOK_DECLARED: REFUSED by the look-window rule first'. The positive control (--cut 2026-01-01) reaches the stub after 1 scratch log line and the marker. Also plan_tests rows 'plan: fix 2: ...' (3 rows) and self_test rows 'guard.fix2 ...' (9 cases). The real val_access.log is unchanged after the children.

done.item: Fix 4 (vhi_guard.py): tokenize and tarfile wrapped; the not-covered list rewritten
done.how: Python 3.13.18 has both names: tokenize._builtin_open and tarfile.bltn_open. install_read_guard now points them at the guarded open, the same way as bz2._builtin_open. This covers tokenize.open (also used by linecache) and tarfile.open in every mode, 'r:' included. The docstring now lists what stays NOT covered: io.FileIO and _io.FileIO, _io.open called directly, io.open_code, os.open (and os.read on its descriptor), mmap; pyarrow's own readers (OSFile, memory_map, pyarrow.fs input files, pyarrow.feather.read_table and pyarrow.ipc called directly, the private modules, dataset fragments); sqlite3 and HDF5; hard links (realpath does not resolve them; a hard link made outside lab/ escapes every lab/ rule); file objects handed to readers; other processes; the re-entrancy pass-through. It also says that numpy.fromfile of a path goes through builtins.open in numpy 2.5, and so do pandas.read_feather / read_orc / read_pickle / read_json and numpy.load. I checked each of these claims on absent paths in a scratch process before writing it.
done.proof: proof_i_guard.json, rows 'refused in process: fix 4 ...' (7 rows, absent paths only). Refused: tokenize.open of a path under results/holdout/ and of a lab CSV; tarfile.open(..., 'r:') of a path under results/holdout/, under lab/data/, and of a lab CSV name; numpy.fromfile of a path under results/holdout/ and of a lab CSV. Also the row 'the guard wraps ... tokenize's and tarfile's captured open (fix 4) ...', and the row 'the refused probes recorded no read, logged nothing and wrote no marker'.

done.item: Fix 5a (vhi_guard.frozen_files_check, look.py plan, vhi_guard.open_run): synthesis A's frozen sha256 checked before the access line
done.how: frozen_files_check takes the frozen values from lab/results/r2/autopsy/synthesis_A.json ('frozen_files_sha256'). It checks the 15 files the look uses: goldlab sim/r2/data/split, r2/recalc.py, r2/fp_costs.json, the 7 strategy files, the F1 model B1_ridge_full.json, and synthesis A's portfolio.py. The proposed_validation_look text must quote the same sha256 for sim.py, recalc.py, fp_costs.json and portfolio.py. Every sha256 quoted in the text must be a frozen value. synth.py is recorded as 'not used by the look' (it is unchanged). The sha256 of synthesis_A.json is recorded: 2897cdf9..., equal to its committed version. A look is refused on any problem, twice: in plan, and in open_run just before log_access. For a rehearsal the check is recorded in meta['frozen_files_check'], not refused; a WARNING goes to stderr if it fails. The marker also records declared_sha256 and synthesis_A_frozen_files_ok.

done.item: Fix 5b (vhi_run.check_first): '@payoff' references that differ from their P0 sleeve shown as WARNING lines
done.how: payoff_reference_vs_sB is now computed before check_first. check_first adds two keys. 'payoff_references': for each '<sleeve>@payoff' reference and each run (fp/stress x lab/live), the window counts, total R, and the orders refused by the 3-spread rule on the whole frame. 'warnings': one 'WARNING (check first; a warning, not a failure) ...' line, with the counts, for each run that is not identical. 'passed' is unchanged; the status gets a suffix only when warnings exist. run_spec prints the warnings after the check-first line, and look.py prints them again after the output is written. In sample all 5 references are identical in all 20 runs, so there is no WARNING. Window trades per reference: F1 ETH 516/514/518/517, ocm4 492 x4, donch4h 207/240/207/241, brk72 BTC 549/558/549/558, orb xau 464/510/464/508. 0 trades only on one side, 0 matched trades differing. Orders refused on the whole frame: F1 ETH x1.5 has 1 (lab and live); all others 0.
